resale_co.name: Resale Certificate
resale_co.issued_by: Township of Saddle Brook Building Department (Construction Official / Fire Official inspection; Property Maintenance Officer checks the exterior)
resale_co.lead_time: Inspections are on Wednesdays between 10:00 a.m. and 2:00 p.m. If fees are paid by check, allow a one week wait for the check to clear. No same-day re-inspections.
requirements: Proof of payment of the $200 water meter fee (Water Department)
Payment of the Resale Certificate fee, a completed application and an approved inspection

Ten-year sealed battery smoke alarms on each level and outside each sleeping area; hardwired alarms (installed after 1995) in bedrooms, near bedrooms and on each story, not replaced with battery units
Carbon monoxide detector within 10 feet of all sleeping areas
Low voltage fire alarm systems tested by a licensed electrician or fire alarm contractor, with the report submitted before the inspection
Secondary power source warning label (generators, solar, battery storage) within 18 inches of the main panel and meter
Property Maintenance Officer inspects the sidewalk and the whole exterior
Open permits are checked on the application

fees.label: Resale Certificate fee
fees.quote: Payment of the $125 Resale Certificate fee*.

fees.label: New application if the closing does not happen within 60 days
fees.quote: If the closing does not take place within 60 days, a new application and $100 Resale Certificate fee must be submitted.

fees.label: Water meter fee on the sale of any home (paid to the Water Department; proof needed)
fees.quote: Proof of payment (copy of receipt) of $200 water meter fee.

resale_co.how_to_apply: Pay the $200 water meter fee at the Water Department (call Donna, 201-587-2905) and get a receipt, then submit the Resale Certificate application with the fee to the Building Department, 55 Mayhill Street, Saddle Brook, NJ 07663 (Monday to Friday 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.). Re-inspections cost the same as the first inspection.
resale_co.contact_title: Construction Official / Building Subcode Official / Zoning Officer / Property Maintenance Official

evidence.quote: The Saddle Brook Building Department must have the following prior to the issuance of a Resale Certificate:
Certificate is valid for 60 days from issue date.
Inspections are performed on Wednesdays between 10:00 a.m.-2:00 p.m.

All re-inspections will be charged a re-inspection fee equal to the 1st inspection fee for each additional time an inspection official is required to return to the premises, per Municipal Ordinance #1512-11.
The Property Maintenance Officer will inspect the sidewalk and the entire exterior of the property to ensure property maintenance compliance.
If you’re looking for information concerning an addition, renovation, alteration, change of ownership or tenancy of your home or business, you’ve come to the right place.

resale_co.notes: The Township's August 2025 Resale Certificate Requirements and Application (Building Department, linked from the Township Forms page) sets the process; the form cites Ordinance #927 (zoning) for the inspection. No Code section was found that states in so many words that a resale certificate is required on every sale, so confidence is medium, though the form and Building Department page treat it as the standard sale document. The form lists $125 in item 2 but $100 for a new application after 60 days. Older 2024/2025 versions of the form on saddlebrooknj.us are no longer online. The Township's email domain is saddlebrooknj.gov while the website is saddlebrooknj.us.

requirements: Ten-year sealed battery smoke alarms on each level and outside each separate sleeping area; hardwired alarms (post-1995) kept and not replaced with battery units
Carbon monoxide detector within 10 feet of all sleeping areas
Low voltage fire alarm systems tested with a report
Secondary power source warning label for generators, solar or battery storage
The August 2025 form no longer lists a fire extinguisher

authorities.name: Saddle Brook Township Fire Prevention Bureau / Fire Official, inspected as part of the Building Department Resale Certificate
authorities.lead_time: Same Wednesday 10:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. resale inspection.

fees.label: Smoke and carbon monoxide detector certificate, per inspection (Code Section 93-10F); reinspections cost the same
fees.quote: Smoke and carbon monoxide detector certificate, per inspection: $50.

authorities.how_to_apply: The smoke and CO check is part of the Resale Certificate inspection; the application grants the Fire Official or Construction Official permission to inspect. Apply through the Building Department.
authorities.contact_title: Fire Official (state directory); Fire Subcode Official / Fire Inspector (Building Department page)

evidence.quote: Smoke and carbon monoxide detector certificate, per inspection: $50. All reinspections will be charged a reinspection fee equal to the first inspection fee for each additional time an inspection official is required to return to the premises.

fire_cert.notes: Code Section 93-10F (Fire Prevention, last amended 2011) sets a $50 smoke/CO certificate fee, but the Building Department's current resale form only mentions the $125 Resale Certificate fee; it is not clear whether the $50 is charged separately or folded in. The August 2025 form follows the 2025 state changes: no fire extinguisher, and a secondary power source label is required.

other_items.label: Water meter fee
other_items.detail: A $200 water meter fee applies to the sale of any home (Ordinance 1472-09); pay the Water Department (201-587-2905) and bring the receipt.

other_items.label: Sidewalk and exterior inspection
other_items.detail: The Property Maintenance Officer inspects the sidewalk and the whole exterior.

other_items.label: Open permits
other_items.detail: The Building Department checks for open permits on the application.

open_questions: Is the $50 smoke/CO certificate fee in Code Section 93-10F charged in addition to the $125 Resale Certificate fee?
Is the Resale Certificate fee $125 or $100 (the form shows both)?
Is there a rush fee for short-notice inspections?
